purpose: Follow a reported prototype from scope selection through checking and repair to a claimed deployment.
observation: Masad holds suggested features, tests despite a completion claim, asks about admin access, then reports deployment.
possible_condition: Ability to inspect a working prototype and request a change before deploying.
rival_explanation: A prepared vendor demonstration can select a tractable task and hide preparation and failures.
discriminating_evidence: Unedited task trace, initial prompt provenance, tests and subsequent use by another person.
analytical_consequence: Count a reported bounded demonstration, not proven production reliability or novice empowerment.

purpose: Examine how generated implementation relates to planning and review.
observation: Masad tests outputs; Shipper reports code review and studying internals; Boris reports plans, auto-accepted edits and later human review, with a prototype exception.
possible_condition: Tasks are inspectable, and speakers possess or can recruit relevant expertise.
rival_explanation: These practices may reflect established professional quality requirements rather than an AI-specific change in agency.
discriminating_evidence: Comparable tasks with and without these checkpoints, including independent downstream error and rework evidence.
analytical_consequence: Distinguish less manual production from less direction or evaluation; do not infer universal human review.

purpose: Challenge a simple claim that either expertise or delegating more always improves action.
observation: Masad warns non-coders can be stranded by migrations; Shipper stresses understanding; Boris reports a newer colleague delegating diagnosis faster than his own manual attempt.
possible_condition: Task failure modes, model capability and the user’s current expectations differ.
rival_explanation: Unequal information or task portions, selective narration and tool-specific capability could explain the contrast.
discriminating_evidence: Matched users and tasks, verified fixes, and records of both initial expectations and recovery attempts.
analytical_consequence: Treat expertise as a possible resource for intervention, not a sufficient or always advantageous condition.

purpose: Examine whether delegation runs only from a person to a system.
observation: Claire changes sales escalation criteria and also lets agents assign her tasks that require physical action.
possible_condition: A person can configure routing and has authority over her own workflow.
rival_explanation: Ordinary automation and reminders may account for the same pattern without a new form of agency.
discriminating_evidence: Records of attempted overrides, refusals and renegotiated priorities, including when the user disagrees.
analytical_consequence: Model direction as potentially reciprocal; a task from an agent does not itself establish coercion or loss of agency.

purpose: Use one user and browser route to test a purely personal-skill explanation.
observation: Claire says browsing YouTube comments worked slowly, whereas queuing Buffer shorts failed despite the page appearing simpler.
possible_condition: Platform, access and task details differ.
rival_explanation: These are different tasks, not a controlled comparison of interfaces.
discriminating_evidence: Repeat matched operations with logged interface states, permissions, failures and subsequent resolution.
analytical_consequence: Bound any skill-based claim by infrastructure and task dependence; Buffer’s eventual ending stays unknown.

purpose: Compare expanded implementation participation with experienced workload and tool selection.
observation: Wen describes polishing code and consulting, wanting to do more than people can keep up with, retaining Figma alternatives and sometimes preferring a direct edit.
possible_condition: More available action can raise ambitions, while particular interfaces make alternatives harder to compare.
rival_explanation: Launch pressure and Wen’s prior Figma experience may explain workload and tool preference.
discriminating_evidence: Longitudinal time and decision traces across equally demanding projects using different tools.
analytical_consequence: Do not equate greater capability, more choice or more output with greater experienced freedom.

purpose: Compare supplying a style standard to AI with asking AI to articulate an implicit standard.
observation: Shipper describes encoding a style guide and sending suggested changes to an editor; Wen describes AI extracting a rubric from her own notes.
possible_condition: Existing explicit rules versus retained material from which criteria can be inferred.
rival_explanation: The generated rubric could be plausible generic language that Wen recognizes without it faithfully describing her decisions.
discriminating_evidence: Compare rubric predictions with held-out judgments and record specific acceptance, rejection and revision of criteria.
analytical_consequence: Evaluation criteria may themselves be partly generated; neither faithful self-knowledge nor hiring improvement is established.

purpose: Examine AI use that concerns the organization of a person’s work rather than executing a fixed task.
observation: Shipper links dissatisfaction with a conventional founder model, asking for writer-founder examples, and a narrated shift toward writing-centered work.
possible_condition: A founder has discretion to reorganize his own work and recognizes possible alternative role models.
rival_explanation: AI may legitimize a pre-existing preference; retrospective business success can motivate narrative reconstruction.
discriminating_evidence: Contemporaneous conversations, alternative influences, actual work-allocation changes and later contrary reflections.
analytical_consequence: Treat reorientation as one speaker’s account; it suggests revising ends, not proof that AI caused business success.

purpose: Test whether checking and withholding release are unique to AI-mediated work.
observation: Masad checks an AI-built prototype; in an account without substantive AI use, Karri tests a reassuring demo, finds defects and delays release.
possible_condition: Someone can exercise quality judgment before a consequential release.
rival_explanation: Tasks, organizations and role seniority differ; dates are not verified.
discriminating_evidence: Comparable workflows in the same organization before and after AI introduction, with verified chronology.
analytical_consequence: Claim a shared practice across AI and non-AI accounts, not historical priority or a new practice invented by AI.

purpose: Challenge a permanent allocation of execution to AI and judgment to people.
observation: Boris reports human review today; Wen uses AI to form criteria and explicitly expects AI judgment to improve while describing present human accountability.
possible_condition: Current organizational responsibility can differ from who contributes an evaluative suggestion.
rival_explanation: Human accountability may be symbolic or imposed rather than a practical ability to intervene.
discriminating_evidence: A disagreement where a person attempts to reject an AI recommendation and can or cannot change the outcome.
analytical_consequence: Replace the simple human-judgment category with negotiation of criteria and checkpoints; accountability alone is not agency.

purpose: Compare reported damage, continued enthusiasm and a separately described operational adjustment.
observation: Claire reports calendar deletion and positive utility, and elsewhere explains task splitting by context overload.
possible_condition: Perceived benefits coexist with failures; resources support continued experimentation.
rival_explanation: Sunk cost, content incentives or selective memory may explain persistence.
discriminating_evidence: Dated records connecting specific failures to specific responses, recovery status and discontinued uses.
analytical_consequence: Do not infer calendar restoration, a deletion-to-role-splitting causal chain, or inevitable abandonment after failure.

purpose: Check what apparently fast production stories include in their time window.
observation: Masad’s bounded demo ends with claimed deployment; Wen clarifies that a ten-day external-release push followed longer internal exploration.
possible_condition: Different starts and readiness standards produce different apparent speed.
rival_explanation: Task complexity, team size and prepared assets account for the contrast.
discriminating_evidence: Complete effort logs including setup, exploration, discarded versions and subsequent remediation.
analytical_consequence: Do not derive productivity magnitudes or compressed learning claims from edited launch stories.

purpose: Ask whether wider participation in shaping work requires AI.
observation: Wen describes involvement beyond mockups; Karri describes broad project responsibility and an engineer’s unrequested refinement without invoking AI.
possible_condition: Organizational permissions and room to exercise initiative can support broad roles.
rival_explanation: Selection of unusually empowered senior or craft-oriented teams may dominate the technology difference.
discriminating_evidence: Employee accounts under narrower job definitions with comparable tool access.
analytical_consequence: Keep role authority and organizational design as unresolved conditions, not effects automatically attributed to AI.

purpose: Distinguish useful alternatives from the number of decisions or controls a tool presents.
observation: Wen values comparing design alternatives and sometimes editing directly; Karri argues that opinionated defaults spare users distracting tool decisions.
possible_condition: Some decisions concern valued outcomes and others concern setup friction.
rival_explanation: These are preferences of different speakers rather than measured effects on users.
discriminating_evidence: Observe which defaults users endorse, which they try to override, and whether overriding is practically possible.
analytical_consequence: Define meaningful revision capacity separately from maximizing clicks, prompts, configuration or manual work.

purpose: Test whether repeated review and correction sustain delegated work.
observation: Aishwarya reports repeated hot fixes ending in support-product shutdown; pilot Shipper/Boris describe review practices without comparable terminal failure.
possible_condition: Multistep dependencies and unpredictable use may outrun local fixes.
rival_explanation: Implementation immaturity, staffing or selected task difficulty could explain the shutdown.
discriminating_evidence: Comparable logged failures with review frequency, repair effort and durable outcomes.
analytical_consequence: Review opportunities are insufficient evidence of recoverability; retain withdrawal as a distinct endpoint.

purpose: Test user prompting against external capability conditions.
observation: Lazar attributes failure generally to users but reports a week-long workaround becoming easy when an API arrived; Eric reports shelving then restarting after a model preview.
possible_condition: Access to a suitable interface or changed model capability.
rival_explanation: Changed task scope or additional user learning could account for improvement.
discriminating_evidence: Same task and user before/after the capability change, including attempts before it.
analytical_consequence: Bound self-blame and skill-only explanations; separate local correction from changes outside the user’s control.

purpose: Locate who can obtain a change in technical constraints.
observation: Farhan reports obtaining larger context through shared provider channels within an hour; Lazar reports an API becoming available after a week of effort.
possible_condition: Organizational provider relationships may change feasible repair routes.
rival_explanation: The same capacity might have been available on request to ordinary customers.
discriminating_evidence: Matched ordinary-user requests, eligibility rules and response histories.
analytical_consequence: Add mobilizing repair resources as an emerging category; privilege is a testable condition, not a verified exclusion rule.

purpose: Challenge both universal novice empowerment and a universal expertise prerequisite.
observation: Zevi combines manual QA and several model reviews but explicitly does not release the demo; Lazar reports a working extension despite technical objections; Eric relays a noncoder CRM success.
possible_condition: Task scope, architectural knowledge and access to other evaluators differ.
rival_explanation: Prepared demos and commercial selection may explain apparent success.
discriminating_evidence: Independent downstream use and corrections by the same novice, including failed attempts and outside help.
analytical_consequence: Retain the thin success countercases; distinguish entry, verification and sustained operation, and disaggregate kinds of expertise.

purpose: Examine continued dependence after creating an artifact.
observation: Lazar reports an enterprise prototype later reproduced by engineers and declines edits by a tool he cannot steer; Eric announces paid human help without a completed rescue.
possible_condition: Production requirements and steerability can shift work toward specialists.
rival_explanation: Tool maturity and preference rather than incapacity may explain the choice.
discriminating_evidence: Work traces before and after transfer, costs, actual help use and downstream reliability.
analytical_consequence: Do not equate initial output with independence or announcements with enacted repair.

purpose: Test manual takeover as a necessary condition of meaningful intervention.
observation: Wu describes an experiment removing the manual fallback and interprets documentation/context changes as a learning route; Farhan advocates human override but gives no enacted paired example here.
possible_condition: Changing the environment could substitute for direct implementation.
rival_explanation: The experiment may simply defer unresolved work; consent and successful outcomes are unknown.
discriminating_evidence: Named blocked features before/after context changes, outcome, and participant ability to exit the experiment.
analytical_consequence: Do not require manual takeover in the theory; do not claim forced AI use has been shown to preserve agency.

purpose: Compare discrepancies in what reviewers count as success.
observation: A client prizes correct email fields while Hamel objects to generic wording; another client treats external benchmarks as application evaluation; a rental trace requires local product context to identify an unavailable tour.
possible_condition: Evaluation depends on task-relevant context and criteria.
rival_explanation: Consultant taste or professional jurisdiction may drive criticism without downstream benefit.
discriminating_evidence: Recipient responses, application-level errors, evaluator disagreements and subsequent outcomes.
analytical_consequence: Presence of human review does not establish adequate criteria; criterion revision is distinct from fixing an output.

purpose: Follow criteria artifacts generated with AI and then modified.
observation: Hamel rejects broad generated error labels, offers more actionable labels and reclassifies notes; pilot Wen reports AI-produced design criteria.
possible_condition: Inspectable examples and authority to revise a rubric.
rival_explanation: Analysts may rationalize preferences; actionable labels need not improve products.
discriminating_evidence: Independent coder use, changes in repair decisions and downstream product traces.
analytical_consequence: Retain reciprocal criteria formation; do not make humans sole authors of judgment or import interviewees’ methodological claims as our protocol.

purpose: Challenge a simple labor-saving account of delegation.
observation: Simon associates parallel agents with exhaustion despite expertise; Wen reports overload; Wu estimates shorter reviews while retaining author attention.
possible_condition: More simultaneous work may expand cognitive demand even as individual tasks shrink.
rival_explanation: Self-imposed ambition, task selection or organizational growth could create the burden.
discriminating_evidence: Time diaries, throughput, new commitments and ability to decline under matched workload.
analytical_consequence: Time per task and total discretionary capacity must be separated; no net autonomy or productivity estimate follows.

purpose: Examine narrowing, selective review and withdrawal as responses.
observation: Simon withholds private data and restricts a tool to a container; Wu describes selective omission of a separate human reviewer; Aishwarya reports shutting down an unmanageable product.
possible_condition: Consequences and inspectability may set distinct delegation boundaries.
rival_explanation: Risk preferences and task types differ; restriction may be imposed rather than chosen.
discriminating_evidence: Actual unwanted actions, boundary changes, who may refuse and associated costs.
analytical_consequence: Less delegation can be an agentic response, but outcome and freedom to choose require evidence.

purpose: Probe worker versus leader discretion and avoid attributing all change to AI.
observation: Aishwarya attributes expert reluctance to replacement fears; Wu imagines unprepared mandated users and discusses performance-review assistance; Farhan recounts a non-AI decision disagreement and costly rewrite accepted by leadership.
possible_condition: Seniority and authority may influence whose criteria and revisions count.
rival_explanation: Founder rhetoric and retrospective justification may dominate these narratives.
discriminating_evidence: Direct reports’ own accounts of contesting a consequential decision, plus decision records and non-AI comparisons.
analytical_consequence: Organizational authority remains unresolved; secondhand fear and hypothetical workers cannot establish experienced employee agency.

purpose: Examine changing specifications during use rather than fixed goals.
observation: Bank underwriters reportedly extend lookup to whole-case comparison; Zevi asks for a technical comparison then challenges the model’s equivalence.
possible_condition: Apparent capability invites new requests and exposes contextual distinctions.
rival_explanation: Ordinary scope creep or learning rather than AI-specific transformation.
discriminating_evidence: Dated task specifications, user requests, system changes and subsequent decisions.
analytical_consequence: An initially workable arrangement can become misaligned through use; review conditions must be reassessed when the task changes.

purpose: Test the relationship among favorable output, checkpoint compliance and effective direction.
observation: Shipper reports an email sent without expected approval that nevertheless matched his intended content; other accounts describe review or interfaces designed to feel controllable.
possible_condition: Routine tasks may yield acceptable outputs without a check.
rival_explanation: A fortunate outcome may conceal unreliable compliance; declared checks may differ from actual behavior.
discriminating_evidence: Repeated matched sends including disagreement, intervention attempts, logs and recipient effects.
analytical_consequence: Separate acceptable result, authorization and perceived control; do not predict every skipped check causes harm or treat satisfaction as proof of agency.

purpose: Compare responses to recurring repair failures.
observation: Shipper obtains two senior-engineer rewrites after patch cascades; Aishwarya reports product shutdown after repeated fixes. Shipper’s engineers also used AI.
possible_condition: Time, expertise and ability to change the diagnosis may alter the response.
rival_explanation: Tasks, systems and resources differ; specialist rewrites may still fail.
discriminating_evidence: Production traces after rewrites and shutdown decision records under comparable task complexity.
analytical_consequence: Add reframing and specialist transfer as attempted alternatives, not proven recovery or a return to exclusively manual work.

purpose: Test whether resource access guarantees successful correction or local work is always insufficient.
observation: A hosted agent service is paused because its harness is hard to maintain; Eric reports restart after capability change; Farhan reports provider unblocking; Sander reports improvement after adding examples and explanations.
possible_condition: Control of dependencies and fit of a local intervention can matter alongside resources.
rival_explanation: Narratives select outcomes; test quality and actual resources are unverified.
discriminating_evidence: Failures and successes with resources measured beforehand and comparable tasks over time.
analytical_consequence: Bound CAT005: resources are candidate conditions, not sufficient or universally necessary causes; retain local repair and resource-rich nonresolution.

purpose: Distinguish dependence arising from inability from chosen allocation of time.
observation: Elena reports building herself then hiring Lazar to expand initiatives; Shipper cites understanding and time; Lazar describes engineering transfer for production.
possible_condition: Task requirements, time and preferred commitments differ.
rival_explanation: Hire narratives may understate skill limitations or organizational obligations.
discriminating_evidence: Compare what each person can do, chooses to do and is required to do before/after obtaining help.
analytical_consequence: Do not infer diminished agency from collaboration; separate technical competence, available time and discretion over work.

purpose: Test whether AI-mediated work can alter what is worth pursuing.
observation: Elena describes prototypes both weakening and strengthening ideas and reports stopping some early; pilot Shipper reconsiders writer/founder identity; bank users expand requests.
possible_condition: Concrete representations may prompt changed goals or task scope.
rival_explanation: Tool limitations may suppress valuable ideas; prior preferences may simply be affirmed.
discriminating_evidence: Compare abandoned ideas evaluated through other media, decision records and later regret or revival.
analytical_consequence: Broaden CAT003 to include pursuing and declining possibilities while keeping identity change thin; prototype effects are not proof of better preferences.

purpose: Challenge inevitable overload and purely imposed-demand accounts.
observation: Elena reports protecting family time and refusing availability; Simon and Shipper report demanding use; Noam describes enjoyment and difficulty disengaging alongside relayed workload concerns.
possible_condition: Position, preferences, workload authority and appeal of the activity may differ.
rival_explanation: Self-presentation or selection may explain expressed balance; refusal consequences are unknown.
discriminating_evidence: Time and demand records plus direct accounts of accepted and penalized refusals across roles.
analytical_consequence: Keep both chosen engagement and imposed demands live; do not use founder burden to prove employee loss or senior refusal to prove universal freedom.

purpose: Test whether more technical capability always better serves a person’s purpose.
observation: Sander reports removal and anonymization of an identifying email lowered prompt performance after a privacy request; Simon limits data/tool access.
possible_condition: Privacy and other commitments may constrain acceptable means.
rival_explanation: Prompt effects may be unstable; final privacy choice and security outcomes are unknown.
discriminating_evidence: Retained variants, repeated tests, final published prompt and decision rationale.
analytical_consequence: Recognize conflicting criteria and attempted value-preserving changes; do not claim the privacy-performance conflict was resolved or privacy prevailed.

purpose: Compare revision of success criteria at user and provider levels.
observation: Nick reports new measurement and public goals after an overly pleasing release; Hamel challenges correct-but-generic email and revises unhelpful error categories.
possible_condition: Evaluation arrangements may reward an output that fails a broader purpose.
rival_explanation: Professional rhetoric or post-hoc justification may explain stated change without better outcomes.
discriminating_evidence: Versioned criteria and tests plus user outcomes, dissent and costs after changes.
analytical_consequence: Criteria are produced at several levels; provider reform is reported, not verified improvement or rollback.

purpose: Bound elaborate prompting and evaluation prescriptions.
observation: Sander reports terse everyday prompts and distinguishes visible conversational outputs from unseen product-scale outputs; Zevi demonstrates multi-model review but does not release.
possible_condition: Stakes, output visibility, scale and task difficulty may change evaluation requirements.
rival_explanation: Expert familiarity makes short prompts look easier than they are; demo setup is selected.
discriminating_evidence: Comparable tasks and repeated downstream outcomes with minimal versus elaborate review.
analytical_consequence: No universal prompt complexity or review volume threshold; workflows must be evaluated by their consequences.

purpose: Compare source types before making claims about employee experience.
observation: Noam relays survey feelings, positive and negative, while acknowledging founder survivorship; Aishwarya attributes reluctance to replacement fears.
possible_condition: Respondent selection, role and question wording may influence what is expressed.
rival_explanation: Aggregate or consultant interpretations can differ from actual behavior and cannot establish individual trajectories.
discriminating_evidence: Survey instrument/raw responses with authorization and direct interviews tracing disagreement and outcomes.
analytical_consequence: Mediated employee concerns complicate leader narratives but do not supply verified prevalence, cognitive decline, causal manager effects or direct refusal episodes.

purpose: Trace directions of AI-assisted evaluation within organizations.
observation: Amol uses AI to prepare feedback about direct reports and to simulate feedback from his own manager; Shipper uses agent-guided team plans for coordination and requires authors to stand behind them.
possible_condition: Access to organizational records and managerial authority may give similar tools different consequences.
rival_explanation: Ordinary self-coaching and administrative assistance may explain uses without changing power.
discriminating_evidence: Specific feedback adopted or rejected, employee awareness/contest, decision records and consequences.
analytical_consequence: Add a relational question about who evaluates whom; no employee harm, empowerment or decision accuracy is established.

purpose: Test whether easier production changes obligations elsewhere.
observation: Amol reports strained PM/design work and a rule assigning smaller-project coordination to engineers; Shipper describes more nonengineer contributions; Dhanji describes more coordination and feature demand.
possible_condition: A growing flow of contributions may shift bottlenecks and task responsibilities.
rival_explanation: Rapid company growth, prior staffing or organization structure may generate the same changes.
discriminating_evidence: Before/after task allocation, workload, contributor choice and matched non-AI growth periods.
analytical_consequence: Introduce turning capacity into commitments as an emerging organizational process; do not infer every expanded responsibility is unwanted.

purpose: Seek contrary organizational voice and limits to voice.
observation: Amol reports a public leadership challenge followed by debate; Elena reports saying no to availability; McCabe reports a fixed rating rule, dismissals and board letters, then high approval in a changed workforce; Farhan reports an unforced non-AI technical choice.
possible_condition: Authority, sanction exposure and organizational change may determine whether objection changes decisions.
rival_explanation: Different issues and narrator positions, survivor selection and promotional accounts confound comparison.
discriminating_evidence: Direct accounts from objectors and departed workers, exact objection/decision sequence and sanctions.
analytical_consequence: Voice, refusal, decision reversal and consequence are distinct; neither universal silencing nor general freedom is established.

purpose: Test AI-only explanations against organizational and non-AI change.
observation: Dhanji explicitly attributes staffing changes to reorganization; McCabe’s return predates the narrated AI opportunity and his turnaround combines cuts, focus, ratings and AI investment; earlier autonomy and non-AI testing also appear.
possible_condition: Business pressure, hierarchy and structural change can shape work independently of AI.
rival_explanation: Speakers may retrospectively separate or combine causes to justify choices.
discriminating_evidence: Dated organization, staffing, tooling and strategy records with multiple participant perspectives.
analytical_consequence: Keep organizational change as a rival and context; do not label turnover AI-caused or claim all revision practices are new.

purpose: Challenge a universal requirement for human intervention at each recovery step.
observation: Dhanji reports Goose switching from failed approaches to AppleScript and completing a focused task; his overnight self-improvement account still needs intervention; Wu discusses context changes; Shipper reports pausing a hosted agent.
possible_condition: Focused tasks and available tool routes may permit autonomous local recovery.
rival_explanation: Vendor-selected success and unspecified errors may overstate reliability.
discriminating_evidence: Unedited traces, independent checks of totals, alternative tasks and ability to interrupt unwanted routes.
analytical_consequence: Allow agents to repair means without human stepwise direction; human agency cannot be inferred or denied from automation level alone.

purpose: Test purpose revision against retrospective accommodation.
observation: McCabe reinterprets personal service to fit AI while acknowledging rationalization; Elena describes prototypes changing ideas; Dhanji asks whether a tool is needed at all; pilot Shipper revisits valued writing.
possible_condition: Material possibilities and business pressure can prompt reconsideration of ends.
rival_explanation: Existing preferences or strategic necessity may be relabeled rather than genuinely reconsidered.
discriminating_evidence: Contemporaneous alternatives, rejected options, who endorsed changed purposes and later consequences.
analytical_consequence: Do not portray revised goals as inherently authentic or better; preserve accommodation as a rival to reflective agency.

purpose: Locate control over context and criteria beyond an individual prompt.
observation: Wu discusses encoding tacit knowledge; Amol notes administrator permissions and protected onboarding references; Nick reports provider metrics; McCabe reports centralized values thresholds.
possible_condition: Permission to edit reference material or evaluation rules can shape others’ action space.
rival_explanation: These may be ordinary quality safeguards or governance rather than reduced discretion.
discriminating_evidence: Actual requested context/rule edits, access decisions, rationale, downstream work and ability to contest.
analytical_consequence: Distinguish owning a prompt from controlling shared context, criteria or commitments; do not assume every restriction is harmful.
